forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / DISA STIG: Invoke-Expression (IEX) executes arbitrary strings as commands and is the primary PowerShell injection vector.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove Invoke-Expression. Use explicit cmdlets or call specific functions by name. If dynamic invocation is required, use the call operator (&) with a validated command name.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03: Invoke-Expression with a variable as input enables command injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove Invoke-Expression. Refactor to use explicit, named functions.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: ConvertTo-SecureString with a plaintext password literal exposes credentials in source code.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Never hardcode passwords in ConvertTo-SecureString calls. Retrieve credentials from secret vaults (Secret Management module, Azure Key Vault) at runtime.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded password detected in PowerShell script.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove hardcoded passwords. Use Get-Secret (Secret Management module) or read from environment variables ($env:DB_PASSWORD).

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CIS Benchmark: Setting execution policy to Unrestricted or Bypass allows unsigned scripts to run, bypassing code integrity controls.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Set execution policy to AllSigned or RemoteSigned. All scripts executed in production must be signed by a trusted CA.

forbidden_patterns.reason: STIG V-222643 / NIST SP 800-52: SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 are deprecated and forbidden.
OWASP A07: Setting an environment variable to a hardcoded password literal is insecure.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Load passwords from a secrets management system. Never set passwords as environment variable values in script code.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03: Downloading and immediately executing remote content is a common malware delivery technique.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Download scripts to a local file, verify GPG signature and SHA-256 checksum, then execute from the local verified copy.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A01 / NIST AC-6: Least privilege violation — adding users to privileged AD groups should be logged and reviewed.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use role-based access control with temporary, just-in-time privilege elevation. Log and alert on all privileged group membership changes.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07: Extracting a SecureString to plain text in memory reduces its security value.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Keep credentials as SecureString or PSCredential objects throughout their lifecycle. Only extract to plain text when strictly required by a target API, and clear immediately after use.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / NIST SP 800-53 SI-7: Dynamically creating script blocks from strings enables command injection when variable content is incorporated into the script text.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace [ScriptBlock]::Create() with a static script block that accepts parameters: $sb = { param($Name) Get-Service -Name $Name }; & $sb -Name $serviceName.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / NIST CM-7: Get-WmiObject is deprecated since PowerShell 3.0, lacks the improved security model of CIM cmdlets, and WMI query strings built with string concatenation are vulnerable to injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace Get-WmiObject with Get-CimInstance using parameter binding: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Process -Filter "Name = '$($name -replace "'", "''")'"

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG WN10-CC-000326 / CIS 18.9.102.2 / NIST AU-2: Setting EnableScriptBlockLogging to 0 disables Script Block Logging, removing the critical forensic capability required by DISA STIG and CIS Level 2.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Set EnableScriptBlockLogging to 1. Script Block Logging must remain enabled in all environments.

forbidden_patterns.reason: NIST SP 800-53 SI-3 / DISA STIG: AMSI bypass techniques disable malware scanning for PowerShell scripts, enabling execution of malicious payloads that would otherwise be detected.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Never bypass AMSI. Ensure AMSI-integrated security solutions remain active. Remove all AMSI bypass code immediately.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A06 / NIST SP 800-53 SI-7: Installing modules without publisher verification or marking repositories as trusted without proper vetting removes supply chain integrity controls.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove -SkipPublisherCheck. Only mark repositories as Trusted after internal security vetting. Use Install-PSResource with signature verification from an approved internal repository.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG WN10-00-000155 / NIST CM-7: PowerShell version 2 lacks AMSI, Script Block Logging, Constrained Language Mode, and other security controls. Invoking -Version 2 bypasses all modern PowerShell security features.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove all -Version 2 flags. Disable PowerShell v2 entirely: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root.
